title: Animal Eyes, 2nd edition, chapters 7 (Apposition compound eyes), 8 (Superposition eyes) and 9 (Movements of the eyes), pp. 157-242
why: The Drive copy came through only to p. 65; these chapters hold the fields of view, acute zones, superposition optics and insect gaze behaviour the views need.

authors: Chatterjee P, Mohan U, Krishnan A, Sane SP
title: Evolutionary constraints on flicker fusion frequency in Lepidoptera
why: Flicker fusion across many butterflies and moths would set the pace of both Lepidoptera views from measurements instead of one swallowtail and a few moths.

title: Fast and slow photoreceptors: a comparative study of the functional diversity of coding and conductances in the Diptera
why: Photoreceptor speed across fly families (fast fliers against slow ones) would set the fly view's pace and say whether hoverflies and crane flies need different paces.

title: Visual field structure in the Empress Leilia, Asterocampa leilia (Lepidoptera, Nymphalidae): dimensions and regional variation in acuity
why: A measured butterfly field of view and acuity map would replace the invented 320 degrees and place the sharp regions of the butterfly view.

authors: Mischiati M, Lin H, Herold P, Imler E, Olberg RM, Leonardo AM
title: Internal models direct dragonfly interception steering
why: Head and body steering during interception would set how the dragonfly view's gaze follows a target.

authors: Olberg RM, Seaman RC, Coats MI, Henry A
title: Eye movements and target fixation during dragonfly prey-interception flights
why: Measured head saccades and fixation would set the timing of the dragonfly view's jump to a target.

title: Morphology and number of Ommatidia in the compound eyes of Solenopsis invicta, Solenopsis richteri, and their hybrid (Hymenoptera: Formicidae)
why: The Red Imported Fire Ant is among Alachua's most recorded ants; its ommatidia count would set the ant view's sharpness for fire ants.

authors: Kelber A, Balkenius A, Warrant EJ
title: Scotopic colour vision in nocturnal hawkmoths
why: The primary source for colour vision in starlight, read here only through a later review; it would confirm the moth view's night colour and its light levels.

authors: Stöckl A, O’Carroll DC, Warrant EJ
title: Neural Summation in the Hawkmoth Visual System Extends the Limits of Vision in Dim Light
why: The extent of spatial and temporal summation at each light level would set how much the moth view blurs and slows as the scene darkens.

title: Binocular stereopsis in an insect
why: The first demonstration of mantis stereopsis, with the distances over which it works.

title: Foveal fixation and tracking in the praying mantis
why: How the mantis turns its head to fixate prey would set the mantis view's gaze jumps.

authors: Nityananda V, Tarawneh G, Henriksen S, Umeton D, Simmons A, Read JCA
title: A Novel Form of Stereo Vision in the Praying Mantis
why: Read here as an abstract; the full text gives the disparity range and timing the mantis view's moving-depth effect would use.

title: Visual control of cursorial prey pursuit by tiger beetles (Cicindelidae)
why: Tiger beetles stop and start while chasing prey; the paper would say whether a beetle variant should show this.

authors: Cronin TW, Järvilehto M, Weckström M, Lall AB
title: Tuning of photoreceptor spectral sensitivity in fireflies (Coleoptera: Lampyridae)
why: Firefly receptor spectra and filters would set the firefly variant's colour, read here only through a review.

title: Firefly Flicker Fusion Frequency
why: The only firefly flicker value known to this sheet; it would set the firefly variant's pace.

authors: Martin GJ, Lord NP, Branham MA, Bybee S
title: Review of the firefly visual system (Coleoptera: Lampyridae) and evolution of the opsin genes underlying color vision
why: A review of firefly eyes: receptor classes, eye types and night sensitivity for the firefly variant.

title: Sexual dimorphism in the visual system of flies: The compound eyes and neural superposition in bibionidae (Diptera)
why: The Common Lovebug is Alachua's most recorded fly; this describes the divided eyes of male bibionids.

authors: Rutowski RL, Gislén L, Warrant EJ
title: Visual acuity and sensitivity increase allometrically with body size in butterflies
why: Acuity across butterfly sizes would let the butterfly view scale its sharpness by species size.

title: Visual ecology and voltage-gated ion channels in insect photoreceptors
why: A review of photoreceptor speed against way of life across insects, for the pace of every view.

authors: Kriska G, Bernáth B, Farkas R, Horváth G
title: Degrees of polarization of reflected light eliciting polarotaxis in dragonflies (Odonata), mayflies (Ephemeroptera) and tabanid flies (Tabanidae)
why: Polarization thresholds for finding water, if a later engine adds a polarization proxy.

title: Spectral sensitivities of photoreceptors and lamina monopolar cells in the dragonfly, Hemicordulia tau
why: Receptor classes by eye region in a dragonfly, for the dragonfly view's upper and lower colours.

authors: Bybee S, Johnson KK, Gering E, Whiting MF, Crandall KA
title: All the better to see you with: a review of odonate color vision with transcriptomic insight into the odonate eye
why: Review of dragonfly and damselfly colour vision, for whether damselflies need their own colour setting.

title: Regional differences in photoreceptor performance in the eye of the praying mantis
why: The primary source for the mantis acute zone (0.6 degrees) read here through Land 1997.

title: Form and Function of Stemmata in Larvae of Holometabolous Insects
why: The review a caterpillar view would be built from, if photos of caterpillars get their own view.

authors: Hammer DX, Schmitz H, Schmitz A, Rylander HG, Welch AJ
title: Sensitivity threshold and response characteristics of infrared detection in the beetle Melanophila acuminata (Coleoptera: Buprestidae)
journal: Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology Part A
why: The fire beetle's infrared sense, for a left-out row if fire beetles get a profile.
